name: The name a worker credential writes under is nobody else's
summary: actor_names.collision is the one rule for a worker credential's actor namespace: its head, case folded, must not be a session actor or a name of that shape, a name on the operator or verifier list, the web service's namespace (the launched one, and http), a name that reads as another, or a name the tracker already holds as an author or assignee. EndpointBackend.actor_standing (endpoint action actor-standing) reads the tracker only when the service asks (item 6), and the issue route answers 422 before anything is kept; at use descriptor_actor_denial and InProcessBackend refuse the same. An export that answers no rows is a host fault, never an empty tracker (item 1); the service answers 503. A credential is judged by the rows once and the outcome kept on it (actor_rows_checked, or actor_rows_refused) by _settle_actor_rows, so later writes read no tracker (item 5). Rows inside an earlier same-name, same-owner credential's lifetime are not held against a renewal (own_intervals; item 3). A superuser may waive the row rule with allow_actor and a required allow_actor_reason; the record carries actor_waived and the audit and listings say who allowed it and why (item 4).
